judgments.reasoning_cat1: The preamble names the parties definitely, though the phrase "shall be effective as hereinafter provided" leaves effectiveness to be found elsewhere and the run-together date line is an OCR/typographical artifact rather than a meaning-changing error. Nothing in the wording itself carries two reasonable meanings.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The deferral to a later effectiveness provision is answered by Section 17 ("effective as of the date first above written"), so the two read together coherently, if slightly circularly. No conflict with any operative term.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The recital is definite as to amount, timing and payee; the only oddity is that an obligation ("Farmee agrees ... to pay") is housed in a WHEREAS clause rather than the operative text.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits comfortably with Section 3(B)(2), which imposes a like $2,000 location fee for each subsequent well, so the initial fee and the per-well fee do not overlap in a contradictory way; the only latent question is recital-versus-operative enforceability.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The reservation is specific — named fee tracts, a 2,000' radius, an identified well — and "all rights associated with" is broad but its object is precisely bounded. Little to construe on its own face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It matches the last sentence of Section 2(D) and the asterisked note on Exhibit "A" excluding the same acreage, so the instrument is consistent on this point.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A plain list of exhibits with a definite incorporation clause; the label "Geological Requirement Letter" differs cosmetically from the exhibit's own heading "Geological Requirements" without changing meaning.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Exhibit "B-1" (Right of First Refusal acreage) is referenced here and in Section 16 but is not distinctly present in the attached plat material, which could leave the ROFR acreage unidentified — a real if modest incorporation gap.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Defining a "completed well" to include a well "plugged and abandoned, if a dry hole" is counter-intuitive but explicit; the equipment benchmarks (tanks, christmas tree) are conventional and definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The defined term is scarcely used: the operative provisions instead speak of a well "completed as a well capable of production in paying quantities, or plugged and abandoned" (3(B), 3(D)), so the definition sits loosely against the operative language without squarely contradicting it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition borrows regulatory boundaries and the "e.g." list (spacing unit, unit for production, proration unit) is illustrative rather than limiting, which is a mild general-versus-specific point but the governing referent (field rules or order of the regulatory authority) is definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 3(A)(1) and 2(D): drilling may occur on a drilling unit only partly composed of Farmout Lands while earned rights are confined to 80/40-acre circles within Farmout Lands, a tension in operation but not an outright inconsistency.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Short, circular but definite: an earning well is one that entitles Farmee to an Assignment under the Agreement's own terms.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It depends wholly on Section 3(D), which conditions the assignment on Farmor being "satisfied" and on a 60-day request, so the definition's content is imported rather than contradicted.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "That portion and only that portion" is emphatic, but "capable of producing in paying quantities" is a classic oil-and-gas phrase whose boundary is frequently litigated, and the clause mixes the right to "operate, maintain and produce ... from any well drilled hereunder" with a strictly acreage-limited production right.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be read with 3(E) (depths earned), 3(A)(1)/(B)(1) (wells may sit on units only partly Farmout Lands) and 2(J) (Unearned Farmout Land), and the interaction of an 80-acre circle with regulatory drilling units leaves genuine room for argument about what acreage is earned.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The catch-all "and other similar burdens on production" following an enumeration (royalty, overriding royalty, production payment) is a textbook ejusdem generis question, though the term is narrow in scope.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The defined term "lease burdens" is never actually used in the operative text (Section 15(A) speaks generally of "obligations, burdens and requirements"), so it is largely inert rather than in conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single numeric depth measured from the surface; unambiguous on its face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 3(E), which caps earned rights at 4,000', and with 3(C)'s reference to losing a well "prior to being drilled to Contract Depth"; the only slight friction is that 3(E) allows 100' below total depth drilled subject to the same 4,000' cap.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "The initial well drilled pursuant to" the Agreement is definite, with only a marginal question about a substitute well for a lost test well.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 3(C) permits a substitute well on the same terms, which supplies the answer for the substitute-well case, and 2(I) keys subsequent wells off the initial test well consistently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition requires that the well "has previously produced" and remains capable of producing in "commercial quantities" — a standard different in words from the "paying quantities" test used elsewhere.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 7(A) imposes shut-in royalties on wells "capable of production (whether or not such well has already produced)," which squarely contradicts the prior-production requirement in this definition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Apart from the OCR-mangled term "subseauent well," the definition is definite: any well drilled after drilling and completion of the initial test well.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 3(B) allows subsequent wells if the test well is completed as a producer "or plugged and abandoned," which fits the 2(A) definition of "completed" including a plugged dry hole, so the pieces reconcile.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A clean negative definition tied to whether Operating Rights have been earned; no ambiguous term to name.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It works with 2(D), 3(B)(1) and 5(B) (partial termination as to Unearned Farmout Lands), and any uncertainty derives from 2(D)'s acreage mechanics rather than from this text.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Gross proceeds attributable to the sale or production from a well" against "the cost of drilling, completing and equipping" leaves open whose proceeds, whether royalty burdens are deducted, and whether operating costs count — a genuinely soft payout definition.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Payout drives the royalty escalations in Section 4.A, where Farmor "reserves the right to escalate," so the softness here has real operative consequences and interacts with the audit right in Section 14 without being squarely contradicted.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The three specifications are dated and mechanical; "Farmee's choice on Farmout Land or on a drilling unit that includes all or a portion of Farmout Lands" is broad but deliberately so.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 13(A) states the Agreement terminates "pursuant to Section 3(A)(2)" for failure to meet drilling commitments, yet 3(A)(2) contains no termination language of its own — the termination consequence lives only in 3(F), a cross-reference mismatch; Section 16 also conditions the ROFR on completing the test well by August 31, 1996 while 3(A) requires only spudding by that date.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The provision says Farmee "shall have the option" to drill subsequent wells and then that "at Farmee's further option, it shall continuously develop" by drilling a minimum of two wells per year — "option" and "shall" pull in opposite directions within one sentence, and "fully developed" is undefined.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 13(A) treats 3(B)(3) as a source of termination "as a consequence of Farmee's failure to meet the drilling commitments," which presupposes a binding commitment that 3(B) itself frames as optional; that is a concrete internal inconsistency of the kind courts must resolve.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Lost for any reason," "mechanical difficulty or formation or condition which would render further drilling impractical or impossible" are elastic standards, and "impractical" in particular has no fixed boundary.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It meshes with 3(F) (default for failure to complete) and 5 (abandonment notice), though the substitute-well right operates as a cure that the notice regime of 5(A) does not expressly address.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "After Farmor is satisfied that Farmee has complied with all its obligations" places an unbounded subjective condition on the assignment, and subsection (2) sets a 60-day forfeiture running from completion while the opening words run the 60 days from Farmor's satisfaction — a mismatch of triggers.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read with Section 4.A and Exhibit "D," the earning mechanism depends on this clause; the forfeiture-plus-plugging consequence also sits awkwardly with 3(F), which preserves rights already earned, and with 5(A)'s notice requirement before plugging.
judgments.clause_name: 3(D). Assignment of Operating Rights - Produce to Earn

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A precise formula: surface to 100' below total depth drilled, capped at 4,000'; no term invites two readings.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 2(F) Contract Depth and with Exhibit "D"'s reservation of strata below a (blank) formation, save that the blank in Exhibit D could be filled inconsistently with the 4,000' cap.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The provision distinguishes automatic termination for drilling failures from notice-and-cure termination for "any other" default, but "defaults, other than above, in the timely and proper performance of any obligations" is a broad catch-all, and the takeover sentence reaching "any well ... which has not yet satisfied the earning requirements" is loosely bounded.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is the only operative source of the termination consequences that Section 13(A) attributes to 3(A)(2) and 3(B)(3), and its automatic-termination limb is hard to square with 3(B)'s framing of subsequent-well drilling as optional; it also cross-refers to Section 6, which is keyed to takeovers under Section 5 rather than under 3(F).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The text contains a garbled clause — "if Farmor's interest in the acreage is less than one hundred percent (100%) or the working interest" — plus a stray "5gross proceeds," and "Farmor reserves the right to escalate" leaves unclear whether escalation is automatic or requires an election and by what notice.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: "Without deductions of any kind" conflicts with Exhibit "D"'s overriding royalty clause, which provides that "Assignor shall bear its proportionate part of any severance tax," and the escalation percentages must be written into an Exhibit D form whose royalty blanks contemplate a single figure.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The mechanics (30 days, 48 hours if a rig is on location, deemed election) are specific; "ceases production" is somewhat open-ended as a trigger but the response regime is clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It dovetails with Section 6 (effective date and salvage reimbursement) and 5(B) (consequence of plugging without approval), although 5(A) speaks of a right "to take over the well" while 5(B) speaks of Farmor's "approval," a slight mismatch of concepts.
judgments.clause_name: 5(A). Notice of Abandonment / Farmor's Right to Take Over

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Without written notification and Farmor's approval" imports an approval requirement that reads as conjunctive, and "fails to give Farmor a reasonable opportunity to consider its options" is a vague standard alongside the fixed periods it references.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 5(A) grants Farmor only a right to take over within a fixed period and deems silence an election not to take over — it nowhere requires Farmor's "approval" to plug, so 5(B)'s approval condition is difficult to reconcile with 5(A).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Estimated salvage value ... less estimated plugging costs" and "as soon as practicable" are soft, and the sentence requiring Farmee to assign "any Operating Rights Earned by Farmor and earned by Farmee" is garbled.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is triggered only by an election "under the terms and conditions of Section 5," yet Section 3(F) also lets Farmor take over wells "subject to the terms of Section 6" — the cross-references do not align cleanly.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Shut in for any reason" (with an OCR artifact) for 45 days or longer, a "$500.00 per well per year, prorated on a monthly basis" payment, and a duty to pay "by the last day of each month any such well is shut-in" combine an annual rate with monthly payment in a way that requires working out.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It expressly covers wells "whether or not such well has already produced," which contradicts the Section 2(H) definition of "shut-in well" requiring prior production and continuing capability of commercial production.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "When possible" is a soft qualifier, but the obligation is minor and precatory in effect, so there is little of consequence to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 7(A) and with the notice regime of Section 10; no other provision makes advance notice a condition of anything.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A long indemnity with an enumerated list followed by "of any kind or character" and "including but not limited to" — broad by design; the arguable gap is whether it covers Farmor's own negligence, which the text does not address.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It complements Exhibit "D"'s assignee indemnity and Section 11's insurance and waiver-of-subrogation requirements without contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Free and clear from all liens" is absolute and short; the only latent question is statutory or operator's liens arising by law.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits against Exhibit "D," which gives Assignor a lien on production for unpaid overriding royalty, and against 15(D)'s bar on encumbering — a modest tension rather than a conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One sentence disclaiming title warranty; unambiguous, and "either express or implied" is a settled formulation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Reinforced by Exhibit "D"'s broader disclaimer of all warranties, so the whole instrument points the same way.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The confidentiality period runs "one (1) year after any such well is completed," and "completed" carries the odd 2(A) meaning (including a plugged dry hole), which affects when confidentiality ends.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It incorporates Exhibit "C" for well data delivery, but Exhibit C addresses obligations to "Operator" and directs data to a different addressee than Section 10(B), a mild coordination problem.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Pure addressee information; no operative ambiguity, and it does not even specify a method or deemed-receipt rule.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Exhibit "C" D.1 directs reports to a different address and a different attention party (Mike Stamper) than this clause (Lester Zitkus), a small inconsistency for a provision that purports to govern "all notices, payments or other correspondence."

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The insurance types are named but no coverage limits or terms are specified, leaving "acquire and/or maintain" the listed policies open as to adequacy.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It supports the Section 8(A) indemnity and does not clash with any other provision of the Agreement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The heading "Modifications and Amendments" does not match the text, which is an after-acquired-interest clause about Farmor's retained interests; "subsequently acquired interest in such lands" and "directly or indirectly by Farmee" are broad and undefined in scope.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: There is no other amendment or entire-agreement provision in the instrument, so a reader looking to this heading for the amendment mechanism finds none — and the clause's extension of the reserved override interacts with Section 4.A and Exhibit "D" without a stated mechanism.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause states only two ways the term ends and gives no outer expiry, and its "until such time as" formulation coupled with "and/or" among the cross-references is loose.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It cites Sections 3(A)(2) and 3(B)(3) as termination provisions although neither contains termination language (that is in 3(F)), and it treats the 3(B)(3) drilling programme as a binding "drilling commitment" although 3(B) casts it as Farmee's option — an inconsistency at the heart of the Agreement's duration.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The audit right is broad but plainly stated; "including but not limited to" precedes examples of payments, a mild catch-all with an obvious genus.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It complements the Section 4.A royalty and the Exhibit "D" monthly statement duty; no other provision limits or duplicates the audit right.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "All obligations, burdens and requirements set forth hereunder or otherwise associated with the lands covered hereby" is an open-ended catch-all whose reach — particularly "otherwise associated with the lands" — cannot be bounded from the text.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It could be read to import lease and third-party obligations not otherwise specified, which sits uneasily with the specific undertakings elsewhere (Sections 8, 9, 11 and 15(B)) and with Farmor's disclaimer of title warranty.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "As nearly as possible to its original condition" and the duty to "settle surface damages" are standards of degree, and the requirement of permission from "both the surface owner and tenant" assumes a tenant exists.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It aligns with the surface-restoration references in Sections 5(B) and 8(A), which impose the same cost responsibility, so the instrument is coherent here.
judgments.clause_name: 15(B). Permission to Enter and Surface Restoration

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short, definite access right "at all times" at Farmor's sole risk; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Exhibit "C" B.5 (witnessing coring, testing and logging) and with Section 8(A)'s allocation of risk to Farmee for its own operations.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The enumerated list (assigned, sublet, mortgaged, pledged, encumbered or subjected to a lien) is specific and the consent requirement absolute; no consent standard (e.g., reasonableness) is stated, which is a modest gap.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Exhibit "D" contemplates that Assignee may assign well interests on notice provided it retains a 25% working interest, which reads as a partial relaxation of this flat prohibition and requires harmonising; Section 17 also makes the Agreement binding on "successors and assigns."

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A dated reporting duty with a defined content; "or on a unit containing Farmout Lands" is precise enough.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It overlaps with Exhibit "C" C.2's production reporting without contradiction, and supports the Section 14 audit right.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It is labelled a "Right of First Refusal" but operates as a preferential right to take a farmout on stated terms, and the condition that Farmee "drills and completes the test well on or before August 31, 1996" is a different requirement from what Section 3(A) actually imposes; "one time" against "during the term" adds further uncertainty.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 3(A)(2)/(3) require only spudding by August 31, 1996 with completion within 45 days after total depth, so the condition stated in this clause cannot be satisfied on the Agreement's own drilling schedule — a concrete internal inconsistency, and Exhibit "B-1" identifying the acreage is not clearly attached.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Shall run with said Farmout Lands" is a significant covenant-running assertion stated in a single clause headed "Execution," but the words themselves are conventional and clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The running-with-the-land language and the binding effect on "successors and assigns" sit against Section 15(D)'s flat bar on assignment without consent, requiring the two to be read together; the effectiveness sentence also answers the preamble's deferral.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short numbered list of deliverables with a fixed copy count; nothing vague.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Exhibit "C" imposes these duties on "Operator," a term the Agreement never defines (the obligor elsewhere is "Farmee"), and Section 3(D) makes compliance with Exhibit C a condition of earning — a definitional gap worth noting.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Thoroughly and timely examine," "properly and timely analyzed" and "qualified wellsite geologist" are all standards of degree, and the text contains the typo "casinn" and an undefined abbreviation "EREX."
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Because Section 3(D) conditions the assignment on compliance with "all geologic requirements as set out in Exhibit C," these soft standards become earning conditions, and the reference to "EREX" rather than the defined "Farmor" is loose.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Significant indications," "adequately tested" and "good oilfield practices" are three successive vague standards with no measurable threshold.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 3(D) makes satisfaction of Exhibit C a precondition to earning operating rights and gives Farmor the judgment of whether it is "satisfied," so this vagueness has direct forfeiture consequences under 3(D)(2) and 3(F).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Routine daily prepaid report ... Monday through Friday ... no later than 9:00 a.m. Eastern Time" is mechanically precise, with only the odd word "prepaid" as a drafting artifact.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 10(A)'s incorporation of Exhibit C for well notices; no competing reporting timetable elsewhere.
judgments.clause_name: Exhibit C - B.3(a). Routine daily report

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Non-routine occurrences such as notification of significant shows" is an illustrative catch-all attached to the vague qualifier "significant," leaving the reporting trigger uncertain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It duplicates in part the notice requirement in B.5 and the abandonment notice in Section 5(A), but nothing contradicts it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The list is broad but each item is a document type, and "pertaining to the subject well" bounds it; the copy count is fixed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: C.1 and C.2 specify different copy counts (one copy, two prints, "THREE COPIES") for overlapping categories, so this clause's flat "two copies" requirement is not perfectly aligned with them.
judgments.clause_name: Exhibit C - B.3(c). Copies of reports

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The list of surveys is presented as a check-box form with stray marks and a blank "Other," so which surveys are actually required cannot be determined from the text as executed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Because Section 3(D) conditions earning on compliance with Exhibit C, an unfilled list of required logs leaves an operative condition indeterminate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Timely notice" is the only standard given, with no period specified, so the required lead time is indeterminate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It parallels 15(C)'s access right and B.3(b)'s immediate-notification duty, overlapping but not conflicting.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause says "one copy of the following (unless otherwise specified)" and then specifies "Two final prints" and a heading "THREE COPIES," and item (e) is an open catch-all ("any other data pertinent") — both a copy-count muddle and a scope catch-all.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The copy counts here differ from B.3(c)'s flat two-copy rule for all reports and from C.2's one-copy rule, so the exhibit's delivery obligations do not read consistently as a whole.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Full information on the completion progress, including one copy of the data listed below" pairs an open obligation with an enumerated list, so the reach of "full information" beyond the list is uncertain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It overlaps with Section 15(E)'s annual production report and with B.3(c)'s two-copy rule, and the copy counts across C.1 and C.2 do not line up.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A delivery address and attention line; entirely definite on its face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It names a different street address and a different attention party (Mike Stamper) than Section 10(B), which purports to govern "all notices, payments or other correspondence" and designates Lester Zitkus — a small but real inconsistency.
judgments.clause_name: Exhibit C - D.1. Delivery of Reports

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A form preamble with blank date fields; the parties are identified precisely and nothing is ambiguous in wording.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the Farmout Agreement's identification of the parties and with Section 3(D)(1)'s reference to Exhibit "D" as the prescribed form.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The granting clause is an unfilled form — well number and acreage blanks throughout — so what is granted cannot be determined from the instrument as drafted, and it also refers to its own "Exhibit A" distinct from the Farmout's Exhibit A.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The acreage blanks must be filled to match Section 2(D)'s 80-acre (gas) and 40-acre (oil) circles, and the form's nested "Exhibit A" reference risks confusion with the Farmout Agreement's Exhibit A land schedule.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A habendum-style term tied to production "in paying quantities" or shut-in status — "paying quantities" is a chronically litigated phrase, and cessation consequences are not addressed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It depends on the Farmout Agreement's shut-in provisions, but Section 7(A) and the Section 2(H) definition of "shut-in well" state inconsistent tests, so what keeps the assignment alive when shut in is unclear; Section 4.A's survival of the override adds a further layer.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A comprehensive warranty disclaimer and indemnity; the enumerated categories are followed by "or otherwise" and "of every kind and character," broad but with an evident genus, and blanks for the well number remain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It tracks Section 9 (no title warranty) and Section 8(A) (Farmee indemnity), so it is consistent with the parent agreement.
judgments.clause_name: Exhibit D - No Warranty and Indemnity

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Necessary or convenient for the operation, maintenance, reworking and production" is a familiar but elastic formula, and the assignment is expressly limited to rights Assignor possesses under its own deeds and leases.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The express subjection to the underlying deeds and leases fits Section 9's no-warranty stance and Section 15(A)'s compliance duty; no contradiction found.
judgments.clause_name: Exhibit D - Assignment of Rights of Way

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The royalty percentage and the product ("from the sale of ___ produced") are left blank, and "without deductions of any kind, except that Assignor shall bear its proportionate part of any severance tax" is internally odd in a clause reserving Assignor's own interest.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 4.A reserves the override on gross proceeds "without deductions of any kind" and provides for escalation on Payout, none of which this single-figure form accommodates, and the severance-tax carve-out here contradicts 4.A's absolute no-deduction language.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short reservation of title granting only "other such rights ... to the extent set forth herein"; the phrase "other such rights" is slightly garbled but the sense is plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 2(D)'s limitation of earned rights to operating rights within defined circles and with Section 9's no-warranty clause.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The provision requires notice before any assignment, forbids reducing Assignee's interest below 25% working interest, and bars assignment of operator rights without consent — clear obligations, though "in any other manner assign its rights, duties or obligations as operator" is a catch-all.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 15(D) of the Farmout Agreement flatly prohibits any assignment by Farmee without Farmor's prior written consent, whereas this clause implies assignments are permitted on notice subject to the 25% floor — the two provisions do not sit easily together.
judgments.clause_name: Exhibit D - Restrictions on Further Assignment

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The formation below which strata are reserved is left blank, so the vertical extent of the reservation is undeterminable from the text.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2(F) and 3(E) fix earned depths by footage (4,000' / 100' below total depth), while this clause fixes them by formation, and the two measures need not coincide once the blank is filled.
judgments.clause_name: Exhibit D - Reservation of Deeper Strata

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A standard successors-and-assigns clause; wording is definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits with Section 15(D)'s consent requirement and Exhibit D's assignment restrictions in the usual way; no specific incoherence identified.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short subordination-to-the-parent-agreement clause with a blank date; unambiguous in operation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It confirms that the Farmout Agreement's terms control the assignment, which helps harmonise the Exhibit D form with Sections 4.A and 7 — though it also means the Exhibit D severance-tax carve-out must yield to Section 4.A, an outcome the instrument does not spell out.
judgments.clause_name: Exhibit D - Subject to Farmout Agreement
